resolvedFromPriorJobs.statement: Descent of `fable_analysis` from the declared frozen Matching baseline 1276d0ca1daece81b5b7b38c8b5f5280046e5077 was unverified, because the commit object was absent from the depth-1 clone.
resolvedFromPriorJobs.finding: After `git fetch --depth=400 origin fable_analysis main`, the baseline commit object resolves and `git merge-base --is-ancestor 1276d0ca... HEAD` succeeds. The audit branch does descend from the declared frozen baseline.
resolvedFromPriorJobs.consequence: The audit's Matching authority claim is sound. Job 1's UE-01 can be closed.

resolvedFromPriorJobs.statement: Only Year Seventeen has a committed matching handoff, yet future-volksgeist and jayz-drake-settle-it both have current Matching-side outputs.
resolvedFromPriorJobs.finding: `architecture/storypackage/tools/build_matching_handoff.py` is not a general builder. Its input and output are module-level constants hardcoded to one package: line 15 `PKG = os.path.join(ROOT, "year-seventeen.storypackage-0.2.json")`, line 16 `OUT = os.path.join(ROOT, "year-seventeen.matching-handoff-0.2.json")`. Its docstring states the same scope. It carries literal story content in the source (line 82 emits a data basis string about a specific chart window; line 253 contains a literal tuple naming a specific artist and claim id). It therefore cannot emit a handoff for another package without editing the source.
resolvedFromPriorJobs.consequence: The matching-handoff contract is implemented for exactly one of three packages. The other two reach Matching without the Story-owned presentation-requirements artifact at all, which is why the harness's `story_handoff` stage has nothing to verify for them. This is a Story-layer implementation gap, not Matching's.

resolvedFromPriorJobs.statement: Year Seventeen: package proposal p-28-28-2 excludes c5-reveal-2.1 while the handoff task 28-28.overlap includes it; proposal p-18-18 disagrees with obligation o-18-18.
resolvedFromPriorJobs.finding: The handoff declares `package.packageId = year-seventeen@7` and reads `year-seventeen.storypackage-0.2.json`, whose internal packageId is `year-seventeen@7`. The manifest's audited Story package is `year-seventeen@9`. The handoff's task boundaries were therefore derived from a package revision two behind the audited one, so a proposal/handoff disagreement is expected rather than contradictory.
resolvedFromPriorJobs.consequence: Boundary disagreements between the handoff and the @9 package are revision skew, not an authoring contradiction within one revision. Job 2's P-9 applies: evidence written against one wording is scoped to that wording.

resolvedFromPriorJobs.statement: `grammar/beat-script-map.json`, used by build_year_seventeen.py to join legacy review beats to script sentences, is absent from this checkout.
resolvedFromPriorJobs.finding: The file is absent from the Story worktree at d5117a6d and from the Matching repo at the audited baseline. It belongs to the same class as the handoff's other cross-repo references: a Matching-repo grammar path consumed by a Story-layer builder.
resolvedFromPriorJobs.consequence: The legacy-beat-to-script join cannot be re-derived or re-verified at the audited commit pair. Named precisely under missingReferenceProtocol; carried to Job 7 for the review-reconciliation question.

summary.interpretation: The upstream contract is strong on semantics, provenance, honesty about unknowns and typographic constraint, and weak on quantity. Matching is told what a number means, which claim it came from, how it should look and what caveats attach to it, but never what the number is, in what unit, computed how, from which row.

typedGaps.title: The handoff contract cannot carry a value's magnitude, unit or basis
typedGaps.ownerRationale: The matching-handoff schema is a Story-owned artifact in djtoler/patterns, so the missing field is Story's to add. The figures themselves are Data's to supply. Neither is Matching's, and Matching must not be blamed for not knowing a quantity it was never sent.
typedGaps.proof: matching-handoff-0.2.schema.json tasks[].data.values[] has additionalProperties:false and property set {valueId, role, anchor, entity, population, display, absence}. storypackage-0.2.schema.json lines 702-722 defines a value object requiring `value` and permitting `unit`, `label`, `entity`, `basis`. Observed: 89 values in the one committed handoff use exactly the keys {absence, anchor, display, entity, population, role, valueId} and never a magnitude.
typedGaps.recurrence: Cross-story evidence verified independently of the single handoff. Job 2's principle P-4 is derived from spans S09 (jayz-drake-settle-it) and S16, S17 (future-volksgeist), two different stories, and its finding F-11 spans S09 and S14. Independently measured here: the storypackage `values` construct appears in jayz-drake-settle-it only (50 occurrences in @3 and @4) and zero times in future-volksgeist and year-seventeen, so structured magnitudes are demonstrably unavailable across packages. The schema defect itself is story-neutral: the handoff schema is one shared contract whose additionalProperties:false property set governs every package.

editorEvidence.quote: 1, 4, and 6 are all great options. if the number of songs is actually 8 or close, option 4 would be perfect. otherwise 1 or 6.
editorEvidence.reading: The editor's template choice is conditional on a magnitude that the contract does not transmit. The right answer is 4 if the count is near 8 and 1 or 6 otherwise. This is the magnitude gap observed as an editorial hesitation, not as a complaint about missing data.

It is retained as an illustration of the gap's real-world cost only.

proposedContractDelta.namingDecision: The property is named `value`, the same name the StoryPackage value object already uses (storypackage-0.2.schema.json line 705). This IS a verbatim reuse of the Story field name, so the proposal and its rationale now agree. The earlier draft proposed `quantity` while claiming verbatim reuse of Story names; that was self-contradictory and is withdrawn.
proposedContractDelta.namingJustification: Interoperability: the handoff builder can copy value, unit and basis across from the StoryPackage value object without a rename or a projection, so the two schemas share one vocabulary and no mapping table has to be maintained. A new name such as `quantity` would require a documented projection from Story `value` for no benefit.
proposedContractDelta.compatibilityImplication: No collision. In matching-handoff-0.2.schema.json the token "value" occurs exactly once, at line 463, as a member of the tasks[].text.fields[].role enum. An enum member string and a property name under tasks[].data.values[] occupy different namespaces, so adding a `value` property introduces no ambiguity and invalidates no existing document. Verified by grep: one occurrence, inside the role enum.

addOptionalProperties.value: number | string - the figure itself; direct copy of storypackage-0.2 value.value
addOptionalProperties.unit: string - direct copy of storypackage-0.2 value.unit

proposedContractDelta.constraint: Require `value` whenever display is `exact` or `rounded`; forbid it when role is `absence`, preserving the existing absence bi-conditional. Leave it absent for `qualitative` and `ordering`.
proposedContractDelta.whyMinimal: Three optional properties plus one conditional. It introduces no new object, reuses the StoryPackage field names exactly, and cannot represent zero-for-unknown because the absence and unknown mechanisms already own that case.

crossRepositoryPinFinding.statement: The only committed Story->Matching handoff carries byte-exact receipts into a Matching repository history that shares no ancestry with the audited Matching baseline.
measurementChain: The handoff's entityRegistry.snapshot pins djtoler/astra-visual-selector @ da8b1755ea6d89a3d23c2fea157e972cee75b869, path grammar/entity-roster.json, sha256 7b6a38a7...b9905.
The handoff's visualTasks snapshot pins the same repo and commit, path grammar/visual-tasks.json, sha256 0dcc1de3...bc4f (declared).

At da8b175 both resolve BYTE-EXACTLY: grammar/entity-roster.json hashes 7b6a38a7...b9905 and grammar/visual-tasks.json hashes 0dcc1de3...bc4f. The handoff's receipts are correct at the commit they name.

At the audited baseline (fable_analysis, which this job confirmed descends from 1276d0ca), grammar/entity-roster.json DOES NOT EXIST; only grammar/entity-roster-source.json exists, hashing bea07385..., a different artifact.
At the audited baseline, grammar/visual-tasks.json hashes a58c8e40..., not the declared 0dcc1de3...
git merge-base da8b175 1276d0ca returns EMPTY. git merge-base --is-ancestor is false in both directions. 10 commits are on main and not in the baseline; 19 are in the baseline and not on main.
Therefore da8b175 and the audited Matching baseline are disjoint histories with no common ancestor.

validatorBehavior.observed: python3 tools/check_handoff.py year-seventeen.matching-handoff-0.2.json exits 1 with 'no local clone for djtoler/astra-visual-selector; pass --repo ...'. Supplying the audited Matching checkout via --repo then raises an unhandled FileNotFoundError on grammar/entity-roster.json from check.fsha (check.py line 30).
validatorBehavior.assessment: Failing closed on an unmounted repository is CORRECT and is credited. Crashing with a stack trace on a mounted repository that lacks the pinned path is a robustness defect: a moved or renamed upstream artifact should surface as a typed validation error, not a traceback.
validatorBehavior.consequence: The only committed Story->Matching handoff cannot be validated end to end at the audited commit pair by any available means.

crossRepositoryPinFinding.correctedEarlierReading: An intermediate hypothesis during this job was that the handoff receipts were stale and that the validator passed anyway. Both halves were wrong and are recorded here so the audit trail is honest. The receipts are byte-exact at their pinned commit, and the apparent clean validator run was a no-op: check_handoff.py's main() iterates over argv paths, so invoking it with no arguments validates nothing and returns 0.
crossRepositoryPinFinding.attribution: shared. The handoff is Story-authored and pins a Matching commit, so neither layer alone owns the drift. Matching is not at fault for the absent path, and Story is not at fault for the baseline being a separate lineage.
crossRepositoryPinFinding.openQuestion: Whether `main` or the frozen baseline is intended as the Matching authority for the Story handoff is a governance question for the editor, not something this job can settle from artifacts. Recorded as UE-13.

mediaAbsenceHandling.acceptanceCriterion: Missing media must not be treated as candidate incompatibility.
mediaAbsenceHandling.architecturalEvidence: pipeline/visualtask_batch_matching.py maintains two independent verdict vocabularies. Template fit uses fitVerdict in {native_fit, adapted_fit, conditional, incompatible, unresolved, no_candidate} (lines 477-487, 727). Media uses mediaResult.availabilityVerdict in {available, unavailable, conditional, unresolved, not_required} (lines 524, 567, 577, 598, 603). The media vocabulary has no `incompatible` member and the template vocabulary has no availability member.
mediaAbsenceHandling.empiricalEvidence: reports/full-visualtask-batch-matching-current.json over 41 tasks: templateVerdicts {conditional: 40, incompatible: 1}; mediaVerdicts {available: 7, conditional: 1, not_required: 30, unavailable: 3}. Three tasks have unavailable media while only one task is template-incompatible, so media unavailability demonstrably does not propagate into template incompatibility.

missingDataNotZeroHandling.acceptanceCriterion: Missing data must not be treated as zero.
evidence: check_handoff.py lines 37-40 run a fail-closed scan over every scalar in the handoff and append an error for any numeric zero outside a span start: 'zero value at {path}: unknowns must be typed, not zero'. The Story layer forbids zero as a stand-in by validation, not by convention.
$defs/positiveCount is oneOf[integer minimum 1, $defs/unknown], so zero is unrepresentable for a count by construction and unknown is a typed object carrying a reason.

The observed handoff uses this: focal.simultaneous and focal.storyItems both carry {"unknown": "the narration does not say how many pre-streaming rappers"} on task 30-30a.main, and unresolved item u-30-30a.main-focal records the same fact with kind=focal_unknown.
data.values[] enforces a bi-conditional between role=absence and display=absent, with a required `absence` reason string, so a missing figure is representable as a stated absence rather than a zero.
check_handoff.py lines 33-35 additionally reject any empty string and any forbidden selection or capacity key, keeping template choice and slot counts out of the Story contract entirely.
missingDataNotZeroHandling.assessment: This is the strongest part of the upstream contract and deserves explicit credit. The gap identified in G-05 is the opposite failure mode: not a zero substituted for an unknown, but a display instruction with no quantity attached. The system is rigorous about not inventing facts and silent about not transmitting them.

The editor names the relation shape as group-vs-group with the two thresholds as the groups. The contract carries role=threshold and a population string but no relation object naming the sides (G-04), so part of the meaning was genuinely absent. However the role, entity and population triples present were sufficient to tell that both sides were groups rather than individuals, and Matching did not use them. Story owed a clearer relation; Matching owed a correct reading of what it did receive.

recurrenceJustification.rule: Every ACCEPTED proposed field must be justified by recurring evidence beyond one story. A gap that fails this test is preserved as an unresolved hypothesis and excluded from the accepted deltas rather than carried as a proposal.
recurrenceJustification.testApplied: For each gap: does evidence that THIS EXACT FIELD is required come from more than one story, or from a story-neutral shared artifact (the handoff schema, the validator, or git topology) rather than from observations inside a single package?

Job 2's principle P-4 is derived from spans S09 (jayz-drake-settle-it) and S16, S17 (future-volksgeist), two different stories, and its finding F-11 spans S09 and S14. Independently measured here: the storypackage `values` construct appears in jayz-drake-settle-it only (50 occurrences in @3 and @4) and zero times in future-volksgeist and year-seventeen, so structured magnitudes are demonstrably unavailable across packages. The schema defect itself is story-neutral: the handoff schema is one shared contract whose additionalProperties:false property set governs every package.

Established by measured git topology rather than by story observation: merge-base between da8b175 and the audited baseline is empty, with 10 commits on main and 19 on the baseline. It affects two of the contract's three required snapshot receipts. The proposed delta changes receipt metadata and Story-owned validator behaviour and adds no new semantic field, so it does not rest on cross-story field evidence at all. `matching` is a supporting owner as the owner of the pinned lineage.

Measured across all three audited packages: two of three have no handoff artifact at all as a direct consequence of the hardcoded builder. This is a cross-story measurement, not an observation inside one story.

A property of shared Story-owned validator code (check_handoff.py lines 43-48), which governs every package identically, plus the measured @7-vs-@9 skew. Not an observation inside one story. `matching` is named as a supporting owner because it consumes the staleness signal.

Cross-layer responsibility is preserved rather than erased: each gap, each affected matrix row and each ledger case carries supportingOwners naming the layers that must supply or consume the contract, and ownerRationale states that accountability follows artifact ownership.
